translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ at Colossae: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ; I pray for you at all times.
When we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus our Lord and the love you have for all the saints,
because of the hope stored up for you in heaven, which you previously heard about in the word of truth, the gospel,
which has reached you. Just as it grows and bears fruit throughout the whole world, so it does among you, from the day you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth,
as you also learned from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Jesus on your behalf,
who also told us of your love in the Spirit.

For this reason, from the day we heard, we too have not stopped praying for you and offering petitions, that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding,
so that you may live in a way worthy of the Lord, pleasing him in every way, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,
strengthened with all power according to his glorious might, for all endurance and patience, with joy,
giving thanks to the Father, who called us to share in the inheritance of the saints in light,
who rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,
through whom we have redemption by his blood and forgiveness of sins by his body,
who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.

For through him everything was created, everything in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities. Everything was created through him and for him.
And he is before all things, and through him all things hold together.
And he is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that he himself may be first in everything.
For all the fullness of the Godhead was pleased to dwell in him.
And through him to reconcile all things to himself, making peace through the blood of his cross, whether things on earth or things in heaven.
And you, who were once alienated and hostile in your thoughts, doing evil deeds,
he has now reconciled through the members of his own body, through his death, to present you holy, spotless, and blameless before him,

if you remain in the faith, rooted and established, and do not move away from the hope of the gospel that you heard, which was proclaimed to every creature under heaven, and of which I, Paul, became a minister.
And now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and in my flesh I fill up what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of his body, which is the church,
of which I, Paul, became a minister according to the stewardship from God that was given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God,
the mystery that was hidden for ages and generations but has now been revealed to his saints,
to whom God wished to make known how great among the Gentiles are the riches of the glory of his mystery, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
We proclaim him, admonishing everyone and teaching everyone with all spiritual wisdom, so that we may present everyone perfect in Christ Jesus.
For this I also labor, struggling according to his power, which works mightily in me.
I want you to know how great a struggle I have for you, for the Laodiceans, and for those who have not seen my face in person,
so that their hearts may be comforted, united in love, and brought into all the riches of full understanding, to the knowledge of God's mystery in Christ Jesus,
in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
I say this so that no one may lead you astray with deceptive words.
For although I am far away in body, I am with you in spirit, rejoicing as I see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ Jesus.
Therefore, just as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in him,
rooted and built up in him and established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in it with thanksgiving.
Beware lest anyone take you captive through philosophy and empty deception, which follow human tradition and the elements of this world, and not Jesus Christ.
For in him all the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily.
And you have been filled in him, who is the head of every authority and dominion.
Through him you were circumcised by faith with a circumcision not made by hands, in stripping off the members of the body through the circumcision of Christ,
buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead.
And you, who were once dead in sins and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made alive in himself, forgiving us all our transgressions.
And through his commands he erased the written record against us, which stood opposed to us. He removed it from our midst and nailed it to the cross.
He stripped the authorities and dominions and openly disgraced them, making a spectacle of them in himself, in his resurrection.
From now on, let no one judge you about eating or drinking, or concerning festivals, new moons, or Sabbaths.
These are shadows of things to come, but the body is Christ.
Let no one deceive you who delights in humility and the worship of angels, pursuing what he has not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,
and not holding fast to Christ, the Head, from whom the whole body, supplied and joined together through its joints and ligaments, grows with the growth that comes from God.
If you died with Christ to the elements of this world, why do you still submit to religious rules as though you were living here in the world?
Do not approach; do not taste; do not come near.
These are all things destined to perish with use, according to human commandments and teaching.
These are regarded as a kind of wisdom, with self-imposed worship, humility, and neglect of the body, but they are of no value against bodily indulgence.
If you were raised with Christ, then seek the things above, where Christ sits at the right hand of God.
Set your minds on the things above, not on the things here on earth.
For you died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
But when Christ, your life, appears, then you too will appear with him in glory.
Therefore, from now on put to death your earthly members. Cast away sexual immorality, impurity, defilement, desire for evil things, and greed, which is idolatry.
Because of these things, the wrath of God comes upon the children of disobedience.
You too once walked in these things, when you lived in them.
But now you too must cast off all these things: anger, fury, malice, slander, and coarse joking from your mouths.
Do not lie to one another. Strip off the old person with his deeds,
and put on the new person, renewed in knowledge according to the image of his Creator,
where there is neither Jew nor Gentile, circumcision nor uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free, but Christ is everything and in everyone.
Therefore, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, put on compassion, mercy, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience,
bearing with one another and forgiving one another if anyone has a complaint against someone. Just as God forgave you through Christ, so must you also forgive.
And above all these things, put on love, which is the bond of perfection.
And let the peace of Christ be established in your hearts, to which you were also called in one body, and be thankful.
For let the word of Christ dwell richly in you, teaching and admonishing one another with all wisdom, with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, and praising God with grace in your hearts.
And whatever you do in words and deeds, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father through him.
Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives and do not embitter them.
Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, so that they do not become disheartened.
Slaves, obey your masters in everything, not with service only when they are watching, as people seeking human approval, but with sincerity of heart, fearing the Lord.
Whatever you do, work wholeheartedly, as for the Lord and not for people.
Know that you will receive from the Lord the reward of your inheritance, for you serve the Lord Christ.
But the wrongdoer will receive according to his wrongdoing, for there is no partiality before God.
Masters, grant your slaves justice and fairness. Know that you too have a Master in heaven.
Persevere in prayer, keeping watch in it with thanksgiving.
At the same time, pray also for us, that God may open for us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in chains,
so that I may make it known, as I ought to speak.
Walk wisely toward outsiders, making the most of the time.
Let your speech always be full of the Lord’s grace, as though seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer each person.
Tychicus, the beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord, will tell you everything about me.
I have sent him to you for this very purpose, so that you may know about us and he may comfort your hearts.
He comes with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother who is one of you. They will tell you everything that is happening here.
Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, sends you greetings, as does Mark, Barnabas’s nephew, about whom you received instructions: if he comes to you, welcome him.
So does Jesus, who is called Justus. These men are from among the circumcised, and they alone have been my fellow workers for the kingdom of God. They have indeed been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends you greetings. He always struggles for you in prayer, so that you may stand complete and filled with all the will of God.
I testify that he works very hard for you, for those in Laodicea, and for those in Hierapolis.
Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas send you greetings.
Give my greetings to the brothers in Laodicea, to Nympha, and to the church in Nympha’s house.
When this letter has been read among you, see that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you also read the letter from Laodicea.
And tell Archippus, “Pay attention to the ministry you received in the Lord, so that you fulfill it.”
This greeting is in my own hand, Paul’s. Remember my chains. Grace be with you. To the Colossians: written from Rome through Tychicus and Onesimus.
